title: Chromatic Polynomials and Planar Graph Colorability
abstract: We prove bounds on the chromatic number of planar graphs using vertex degree lemmas.

sections.heading: 1. Graph Preliminaries
sections.text:
Definition 1.1. A graph G = (V, E) is planar if it can be embedded in the plane without edge crossings.
Example 1. The complete bipartite graph K_{3,3} is non-planar.
Remark 1. Planar graphs satisfy Euler's formula V - E + F = 2.

sections.heading: 2. Coloring Theorems
sections.text:
Lemma 2.1. Every planar graph contains a vertex of degree at most 5.
Theorem 3.1. Theorem 3.1 follows from Lemma 2.1. Every loopless planar graph is 5-colorable.
Proof of Theorem 3.1. Using Definition 1.1 and Lemma 2.1, we perform induction on the number of vertices.
Corollary 3.2. By Theorem 3.1, planar graphs have chromatic number chi(G) <= 5.
